title: The Normalised Wigner Negativity Rate as a Second-Moment Probe of Infall in AdS$_3$
abstract: In spread complexity, the average position of an operator along its Krylov chain, recovers the right radial momentum of an infalling particle in AdS, yet it is a measure of the first moment, irrespective of the spread of the wavepacket away from its classical trajectory. The rate of a normalized Krylov-Wigner negativity can be proposed as a diagnostic of the second moment of the boundary state that captures this spreading. Starting with the \emph{seed-normalized} Krylov-Wigner distribution -- that is, the Wigner transform of the descendant cloud, with the decaying return amplitude divided out -- we obtain an analytic Bessel form in the macroscopic limit and compute its total negativity explicitly. Retaining the Bessel variable all the way through, we find that the negativity goes as $\sinh^{4Δ}(πt/β)$, while the raw, seed-normalized state negativity saturates, as dictated by the $O(\sqrt{D})$ bound. Using the exact negative binomial statistics of the Krylov chain and the momentum dictionary of Caputa et al.~\cite{Caputa:2024}, the rate of the negativity scales as the growth rate of the Krylov variance at late time asymptotics \emph{if and only if} $Δ=1$, the Breitenlohner-Freedman saturating dimension in $AdS_3$. This dimensionality is special in that the negativity rate is the product of the proper radial position and momentum, $\mathcal{R} \propto \mathcal{C} P_ρ$, i.e., the rate of the tidal stretch of nearby geodesic falling into the horizon. We comment on the direction for future research, in particular the interpretation of the transverse string size operator in terms of the Krylov number operator through the common $SU(1,1)$ discrete series.
summary: This paper develops the use of the normalized Wigner negativity rate as a diagnostic tool to probe the second moment of quantum wavepacket spreading in AdS$_3$. By analyzing this rate, the authors establish that it directly measures the rate of tidal stretching experienced by nearby infalling geodesics when the system dimension matches the critical Breitenlohner-Freedman value.
main_problem: The research aims to move beyond first-moment diagnostics (like spread complexity) to probe higher moments of quantum dynamics, specifically using the normalized Wigner negativity rate.
main_result: The negativity rate matches the growth rate of the Krylov variance if and only if the dimension $\Delta$ equals 1, which corresponds physically to the rate of tidal stretching of infalling geodesics in AdS$_3$.
method: The analysis employs techniques from quantum information theory (Wigner negativity) applied to dynamics generated by a local operator quench on a CFT dual to an AdS black hole.
model_or_system: The system is modeled using the Krylov chain derived from a holographic CFT, whose evolution is governed by an effective Hamiltonian exhibiting $\mathfrak{su}(1, 1)$ symmetry. The statistics of the resulting occupation numbers follow a Negative Binomial Distribution.

important_parameters: The conformal dimension $\Delta$, the time scale $t/ eta$, and the Breitenlohner-Freedman dimension ($\Delta=1$) are crucial parameters.
main_assumptions: Key steps involve conjectures relating string operators to Krylov chain operators, and the analysis relies on specific asymptotic limits (macroscopic limit) and approximations for mode sums.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the inadequacy of first moments, then introducing the negativity rate as a second-moment probe. It develops the $\mathfrak{su}(1, 1)$ structure leading to Negative Binomial statistics, and finally connects this quantum diagnostic to geometric observables like tidal stretching in AdS$_3$.
why_interesting: The connection between higher-order quantum measures (negativity) and classical gravitational dynamics (tidal forces/geodesics) provides a powerful, non-standard tool for testing holographic duality predictions.
